What does network functions virtualization (NFV) do?
It runs network functions such as firewalls and routers as software on standard servers instead of dedicated hardware
It combines several physical cables into one
It assigns VLANs to wireless clients
Which of the following is an example of a virtual network function (VNF)?
A firewall running as a virtual machine
What is the PRIMARY business benefit of NFV?
It reduces hardware costs and speeds up deployment of network services
It eliminates the need for any network security
It removes the need for IP addressing
An ISP wants to deploy firewall services for new customers within minutes instead of shipping hardware. Which technology supports this?
On what type of hardware do virtual network functions typically run?
Commercial off-the-shelf (COTS) servers with a hypervisor
Which component manages the life cycle of VNFs, including deployment, scaling, and removal?
The compute, storage, and network resources, physical and virtual, that host VNFs
How does NFV differ from software-defined networking (SDN)?
NFV virtualizes network functions; SDN separates the control plane from the data plane for centralized control
SDN virtualizes firewalls; NFV centralizes routing tables only
NFV is used only for wireless networks
Which statement BEST describes service chaining in an NFV environment?
Traffic is steered through a sequence of VNFs, such as a firewall, then an IPS, then a load balancer
DHCP leases are renewed in order
A company runs its router, firewall, and WAN optimizer as virtual machines on one server at a branch. What is a key risk?
A failure of the host server can take down all of those network functions at once
The functions can no longer be managed
Which is a key consideration when sizing hardware for VNFs?
CPU, memory, and network throughput needed by each virtual function
The color of the server chassis
How does NFV improve scalability compared with physical appliances?
More VNF instances can be started when demand rises and removed when it falls
Each VNF must be installed manually by a technician on site
A telecom provider replaces dedicated hardware at cell sites with virtualized functions on standard servers. Which technology is this?
Which of the following is NOT typically delivered as a virtual network function?
Which component provides the virtualization layer that allows multiple VNFs to share one physical server?
What does a virtual switch (vSwitch) do in an NFV host?
It connects virtual machines and VNFs to each other and to the physical network
Which technology lets a VNF bypass the hypervisor's virtual switch for higher network performance?
An administrator notices a virtual firewall's throughput is much lower than the hardware model it replaced. What should be checked FIRST?
The CPU, memory, and NIC resources allocated to the VNF
Which of the following BEST describes the relationship between NFV and cloud computing?
NFV uses virtualization and cloud principles to deliver network services on demand
NFV prevents the use of cloud services
Cloud computing requires physical firewalls only
A company wants to test a new firewall vendor without buying hardware. Which approach is BEST?
Deploy the vendor's firewall as a virtual appliance in a lab
How does NFV help reduce vendor lock-in?
Functions from different vendors can run on the same standard hardware
It requires a single vendor for all hardware
It removes the need for software updates
What is a common concern when moving physical appliances to NFV?
Ensuring predictable performance on shared hardware
Which statement about VNF high availability is TRUE?
VNFs can be run in redundant pairs on separate hosts to avoid a single point of failure
VNFs automatically survive any host failure
Which standards body developed the reference architecture for NFV?
A cloud provider offers firewalls, NAT gateways, and load balancers that customers create through a web console. Which concept makes this possible?
Which term describes a VNF that is broken into small, independently deployable parts running in containers?
Which benefit of NFV is MOST related to energy and space savings?
Consolidating many appliances onto fewer servers
In an NFV design, where do VNFs get their network connectivity to the physical network?
Through virtual NICs connected to virtual switches and the host's physical NICs
Directly through a patch panel without NICs
An administrator needs to add a WAN optimizer at 30 branches quickly. Each branch already has a general-purpose server. Which approach is BEST?
Deploy a virtual WAN optimizer on each branch server
Ship a physical appliance to each branch
What does orchestration provide in an NFV environment?
Automated deployment and coordination of VNFs and their resources
Which of the following is a security consideration specific to NFV?
Protecting the hypervisor, since compromising it could affect every VNF on the host
Using plenum cable in the ceiling
How are VNFs typically updated compared with physical appliances?
By deploying new software images, often without on-site visits
What does 'elastic' scaling of VNFs mean?
Instances are added or removed automatically as demand changes
Which statement BEST describes a virtual router?
Routing software running in a VM or container that performs the same functions as a hardware router
A router that works only with Wi-Fi
A cable that carries routing data
Which statement about NFV and physical network infrastructure is TRUE?
NFV still requires physical servers, switches, and cabling underneath
NFV eliminates the need for NICs
A virtual load balancer is overloaded during peak hours. Which NFV capability addresses this?
Scaling out by deploying additional load balancer instances
Which of the following is an advantage of NFV for disaster recovery?
VNF images and configurations can be quickly redeployed at another site
Physical appliances must be shipped to the new site
Which term describes the physical server hardware used to host VNFs?
What is the main purpose of a virtual network interface card (vNIC)?
To give a virtual machine or VNF a network connection
Which statement BEST compares a physical firewall and a virtual firewall?
Both enforce rules, but the virtual firewall runs as software on shared hardware
Only the physical firewall can filter traffic
Only the virtual firewall can use rules
The virtual firewall cannot inspect packets
Which statement about licensing for VNFs is MOST accurate?
VNFs usually still require vendor software licenses, often based on throughput or instances
VNFs are licensed by cable length
Licenses are tied to the SSID
A network architect wants to place a virtual IPS between two virtual machines on the same host. How is traffic directed through it?
By configuring the virtual switching and service chaining so traffic passes through the IPS VNF
Which monitoring challenge is MORE likely in NFV environments than with physical appliances?
Traffic between VNFs on the same host may not pass through physical monitoring points
Which statement about NFV and SDN used together is TRUE?
SDN can automatically steer traffic through VNFs that NFV deploys
A company migrates its edge router to a VNF. What should be verified before going live?
That the VNF meets throughput, feature, and redundancy requirements
That the DNS TTL is 24 hours
Which statement BEST describes the 'virtualized' part of NFV?
The network function is separated from the hardware it runs on
The network has no physical connections
Which group of appliances is MOST commonly virtualized with NFV?
Firewalls, routers, load balancers, and WAN optimizers
Patch panels, keystone jacks, and cable trays
A virtual firewall instance crashes, and a standby instance on another host takes over. Which design principle is demonstrated?
Which statement about NFV performance is TRUE?
Performance depends on the host hardware and on how resources are allocated to each VNF
Performance depends only on cable length
A company replaces its branch office firewall appliances with firewall software running on the branch servers it already owns. What is the MAIN benefit?
Lower hardware cost and faster deployment of new branches
No need to maintain firewall rules
